name: NextDecade Corporation

profile.description: NextDecade Corporation develops and constructs the Rio Grande LNG natural gas liquefaction and export facility near Brownsville, Texas, along with an associated carbon capture and storage project. The company is pre-revenue: Trains 1 and 2 were 74% complete as of mid-2026, first gas into the facility is expected before year-end 2026, and first LNG from Train 1 is now guided for Q2 2027 with substantial completion in Q3 2027. Matthew Schatzman has led the company as CEO since 2018.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): NextDecade has taken Rio Grande LNG from a development concept to a multi-train construction project - Q2 2026 materials model distributable cash flow from Train 1 start-up through Train 5 completion, and the company refinanced roughly $4.6B of project bank borrowings with a $1B term loan and $3.5B of senior secured notes [1][2]. This is a significant transformation from a development shell to an infrastructure builder, though no train is yet operating. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI deployment or quantified AI savings were found [3]. Market Share (1/2): Rio Grande will be a meaningful U.S. LNG export platform, but NextDecade is a new entrant behind incumbents such as Cheniere with no operating share yet. Pipeline (2/2): Specific milestones with dates - first gas before year-end 2026, Train 1 first LNG in Q2 2027, substantial completion in Q3 2027 (a quarter ahead of the guaranteed schedule), and projected ~$2.0B of distributable cash flow at a $2.00/MMBtu margin [1][2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FY2025 R&D was $8.0M, minimal and not meaningful against a pre-revenue base [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): NextDecade describes itself as building LNG and carbon capture infrastructure to supply lower-carbon energy globally, and its careers materials frame culture as the foundation of how work gets done - clear about what it does, but not distinctive versus other LNG developers [3][5]. Community Impact (0/2): No quantified community investment program was found; instead, local groups and the Carrizo/Comecrudo Tribe have contested the project and said they were not consulted, and a D.C. Circuit court in 2024 ordered FERC to reconsider community impacts [5]. Employee Retention (1/2): Leadership has been stable, with Schatzman as CEO since 2018 and now Chairman and CEO, but no turnover or tenure data was found [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying in the last 12 months was found.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 3 of 7 growth metrics; revenue growth, 5yr revenue CAGR, and profit margin are excluded because the company has reported zero revenue every year from 2020 through 2025, and Forward PEG is unavailable [4]. Debt-to-equity of 326% is above the 300% floor (0.0), and ROE scores 0 at 2x weight - FMP reports TTM ROE of -314.5% against an FY2025 net loss attributable to common of $306M (Yahoo's +13.6% figure reflects consolidated income including non-controlling interests and non-operating gains, so the provider figure for common holders was used) [4][6]. Forward P/E of 7.9 on post-start-up earnings estimates scores 1.0. Weighted 1.0/4 = 2.5, rounded up to 3. Liquidity floor cleared: 2.68M avg volume x $7.38 = $19.8M daily [6].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Rio Grande LNG is physical energy infrastructure - liquefaction trains, storage tanks, and marine loading under long-term offtake contracts - that AI cannot substitute, and rising power demand from AI data centers is a structural tailwind for global natural gas consumption [1][2]. No analyst commentary flags AI displacement risk for LNG export terminals. AI Opportunity (0/1): NextDecade generates no revenue at all yet, and no AI-related revenue or AI deployment was found [3][4].

infinite_game.summary: NextDecade has shown real persistence - surviving years of delays, financing hurdles, and a 2024 court vacatur of its FERC approval to reach construction on five trains. But through Sinek's lens, persistence on a single project is not the same as a Just Cause. The company's purpose reads as building and monetizing an LNG terminal, its community relationships are contested, and it has not yet faced the test of operating and evolving a business.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The stated aim of supplying lower-carbon energy via LNG and carbon capture exists, but it reads as positioning rather than a cause people sacrifice for; the company's own filings acknowledge its carbon capture project may not satisfy ESG-focused investors [5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is solid (Schatzman CEO since 2018), and the small team has executed a complex financing and construction program without disruptive turnover [3]. No evidence of exceptional empowerment or tenure was found, so this is adequate rather than high trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found framing Gulf Coast LNG peers as benchmarks to learn from; the competitive narrative is about securing offtake and reaching first LNG [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): NextDecade has evolved from a development-stage company into a builder-owner of a five-train export complex and added a carbon capture project to the facility plan [1][3]. It remains a single-asset business, so the adaptation is incremental rather than a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): After the D.C. Circuit set aside FERC's approval in August 2024, Schatzman publicly committed to fight to keep Rio Grande on track rather than retreat, and the company has kept expanding the project [5]. That courage, however, is in service of the asset rather than a broader cause.

investment_thesis: NextDecade is approaching the transition from developer to cash-generating LNG operator. Trains 1 and 2 were 74% complete as of mid-2026 with all major Train 1 equipment installed; first gas is expected before year-end 2026, Train 1 first LNG in Q2 2027, and substantial completion in Q3 2027 - a quarter ahead of the guaranteed schedule [1][2]. Management projects roughly $2.0B of distributable cash flow from Train 1 start-up through Train 5 completion at a $2.00/MMBtu margin, and the company refinanced about $4.6B of bank borrowings with a $1B term loan and $3.5B of senior secured notes [2]. At a $2.0B market cap and a forward P/E of 7.9, the market is pricing meaningful execution risk ahead of start-up [6]. Global LNG demand, supported by AI-driven power consumption and energy-security buying, underpins long-term contracted volumes.
thesis_continued: The bear case is leverage and timing. Enterprise value of about $14.0B dwarfs the $2.0B equity value, D/E is 326%, the current ratio is 0.36, and FY2025 interest expense was $170M against zero revenue and a $306M net loss to common [4][6]. Guidance for first LNG has already slipped from 'first half 2027' to Q2 2027, and further commissioning delays would push out cash flows while interest accrues [1][2]. Legal and community opposition persists - a 2024 court decision vacated the project's FERC approval pending reconsideration of community impacts - and a global LNG supply wave from new U.S. and Qatari capacity late this decade could compress the margins assumed in the $2.00/MMBtu projection [5].
key_catalysts: First gas into Rio Grande LNG before year-end 2026 and Train 1 first LNG in Q2 2027, marking the shift to revenue [1]
Train 1 substantial completion in Q3 2027, a quarter ahead of the guaranteed schedule, starting long-term contracted cash flows [1]
Delivery on the ~$2.0B distributable cash flow projection from Train 1 start-up through Train 5 completion [2]
key_risks: Heavy leverage (D/E 326%, EV ~$14.0B vs. $2.0B market cap, current ratio 0.36) with $170M of FY2025 interest expense and no revenue until 2027 [4][6]
Schedule slippage - first LNG guidance has moved from first half 2027 to Q2 2027 - and commissioning risk on a first-of-its-kind facility for the company [1][2]
Ongoing regulatory and community challenges, including the 2024 D.C. Circuit vacatur of FERC approval and environmental-justice opposition [5]
